name: Ethiopia
region: Tigray, Amhara, Oromia, Afar — multi-regional conflict
summary: Ethiopia is experiencing multiple simultaneous armed conflicts behind near-total media blackout. While the Tigray war formally ended in 2022, Eritrean forces remain in occupied areas, federal forces and Fano militia are clashing in Amhara with documented drone strikes on civilians, fighting continues in Oromia, and 18.9 million people are in humanitarian need.
context:
Ethiopia's humanitarian catastrophe is one of the most undercovered of any large-scale crisis in the world. While international attention briefly focused on the Tigray war (2020–2022), the formal ceasefire has not ended atrocity. Eritrean forces remain in occupation of significant areas of Tigray, committing documented human rights violations. Over one million Tigrayans remain in protracted displacement with no safe conditions for return.

A new front of fighting opened in Amhara in 2023 and escalated sharply through 2025, pitting federal forces against the Fano militia — an armed movement that coalesced in response to what Amhara communities saw as federal abandonment. Drone strikes on civilian areas in Amhara have been documented, including a February 2025 strike that killed 16 people including children. The Ethiopian government has imposed a near-total media blackout on both the Amhara and Oromia conflicts, making independent verification extremely difficult.

In Oromia, fighting between federal forces and the Oromo Liberation Army continues across vast rural areas, generating ongoing displacement and human rights abuses on multiple sides.

The humanitarian scale is enormous: 18.9 million people in need, 3.3 million IDPs, and malnutrition at critical levels. In some woredas of Tigray, the global acute malnutrition rate exceeds 19.8% — above the emergency threshold. Over 8.3 million children are out of school across conflict-affected regions.

Massive US aid cuts in 2025 have devastated Ethiopia's humanitarian response, closing 422 health facilities. What is happening in Ethiopia is a large-scale, multi-front humanitarian emergency that the world has largely stopped watching.

donate.name: UNICEF Ethiopia
donate.description: Treating severely malnourished children, providing vaccines, and supporting education for millions of out-of-school children across Ethiopia's conflict zones.

donate.name: ICRC — Ethiopia
donate.description: Providing emergency healthcare and protection services in conflict-affected areas of Tigray, Amhara, and Oromia.

donate.name: IOM Ethiopia
donate.description: Supporting internally displaced people with emergency shelter, water, sanitation, and tracking displacement movements across Ethiopia.

awareness: Share that multiple armed conflicts are ongoing in Ethiopia right now — in Tigray, Amhara, and Oromia simultaneously — with almost no international media coverage
Highlight that Eritrean forces remain in Tigray despite the formal ceasefire, committing documented atrocities with no accountability
Amplify reporting from Ethiopian journalists and diaspora media outlets that are documenting what is happening despite government media restrictions
Raise awareness that 8.3 million Ethiopian children are out of school due to conflict — one of the highest totals anywhere in the world
Challenge media blackout narratives — demand that outlets covering Africa allocate resources to Ethiopia's multiple simultaneous emergencies
political: Urge your government to demand Eritrea's withdrawal from Ethiopian territory as a condition of continued diplomatic engagement
Push for an independent UN investigation into alleged war crimes and drone strikes on civilians in Amhara and Oromia
Advocate for restored and increased humanitarian funding to Ethiopia after devastating aid cuts gutted the response in 2025
Support calls for accountability mechanisms for all parties to the Tigray conflict, including the Ethiopian federal government and Eritrea
Demand that press freedom in Ethiopia be restored — journalists must be allowed to document and report on active conflicts without persecution
